CFML Language Reference: Functions

ArrayNew

Creates a new, empty array. Arrays in CFML grow automatically as you assign elements, so you do not declare a size, only the number of dimensions.

Category

Array functions

Syntax

ArrayNew(dimension)

Parameters

dimension
1, 2 or 3. Any other number throws an Expression exception ("Invalid array dimension").

Returns

A new, empty array.

Usage

Array positions start at 1. Assign elements with bracket notation: <CFSET Names[1] = "Ann">, or for two dimensions <CFSET Grid[2][3] = "x">.

Unlike structures, arrays are copied when you assign them: after <CFSET B = A>, changing B does not change A. Array literals such as [1, 2, 3] did not exist yet in 1999; use ArrayNew plus assignments, or ListToArray.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFSET Week = ArrayNew(1)>
<CFSET Week[1] = "Monday">
<CFSET Week[2] = "Tuesday">
<CFSET Week[3] = "Wednesday">

<CFSET Copy = Week>
<CFSET Copy[1] = "Blue Monday">

<CFOUTPUT>
<P>Week has #ArrayLen(Week)# elements; IsArray(Week) is #IsArray(Week)#.</P>
<P>Week[1] = #Week[1]#<BR>
Copy[1] = #Copy[1]# (assignment made a separate copy)</P>
</CFOUTPUT>

See also

ArrayLen, ArrayAppend, IsArray, ListToArray, Duplicate
